meta.title: Green Building in a Colorado Deal
meta.note: Every figure on this page is quoted from the source named with it. QAP quotes are checked against the QAP text in data/audit/chfa-qap-watch.json.

entries.title: A green certification on every project
entries.finding: Every federal and state tax credit project must certify under Enterprise Green Communities (EGC), LEED or the National Green Building Standard (NGBS). The applicant picks the program.
quotes: CHFA requires all projects to obtain green building certification and accepts several certification programs.

entries.title: When each step is due
entries.finding: Name the program on CHFA's election form at Preliminary Application, show registration at Carryover (or the state credit milestone), and prove certification at Final Application, before the federal credit forms are issued.
quotes: indicating which certification program the project will pursue (EGC, LEED, or NGBS) at Preliminary Application.
Submit evidence of project registration under EGC, LEED, or NGBS at Carryover Application or state credit Milestone documentation.
Provide proof of EGC, LEED, or NGBS certification at Final Application and before issuance of 8609(s).

entries.title: EV-ready parking
entries.finding: With more than 10 parking spaces, 10 percent of the lesser of total spaces or total units must be EV-ready; with 10 or fewer, one space. A circuit and a junction box or outlet count; chargers are not required.
quotes: For projects with 10 or fewer parking spaces, at least one parking space must be EV-ready. • For projects with more than 10 parking spaces, 10 percent of the lesser of total spaces or total units must be EV-ready.

entries.title: Who skips the EV rule
entries.finding: Projects that are 100 percent for people experiencing homelessness or Special Populations, and acquisition/rehab projects, are exempt from the EV-ready count.
quotes: All projects (excepting 100-percent for Persons experiencing Homelessness or Special Populations and acquisition/rehab projects) must have a minimum number of EV-ready parking spaces.

entries.title: Report energy use every year
entries.finding: Once built, every building reports its energy use each year in ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager, a free tool.
quotes: all buildings are required to annually assess and report energy performance using the free

entries.title: Water-wise landscaping
entries.finding: New construction uses water-wise landscaping and limits irrigated turf.
quotes: While meeting design codes, new construction projects shall apply “Water-Wise” landscaping and limit irrigated turf to promote quality of life and climate resilience.

entries.title: All-electric claims need a third party
entries.finding: If the application says the project is all-electric or Electrification-Ready, a third-party energy consultant, architect or electrical designer must describe how.
quotes: If applicable, the Applicant must provide a narrative to describe construction and/or renovation measures demonstrating an Electrification-Ready or All-Electric project from a third-party energy consultant, architect, or electrical design team.

entries.title: No points, but more competitive
entries.finding: Green building earns no scoring points. Going beyond the required certification, or building Electrification-Ready, is “considered more competitive” under a Guiding Principle. CHFA names an efficient, all-electric, net-zero-carbon project as the strongest answer.
quotes: While not required, a project achieving a higher level of energy efficiency certification in addition to the required green building certification or constructing to be Electrification-Ready is considered more competitive as the project would meet a Guiding Principle

The most competitive response to achieving a higher level of energy efficiency is a highly efficient, all electric project certifying to a program requiring net zero carbon emission or net zero carbon emissions ready.

entries.title: Higher programs CHFA names
entries.finding: DOE Efficient New Homes, Phius or PHI Passive House, and, new in the Third Draft, Enterprise Green Communities Plus (EGC+). The plan in force names the first three.
quotes: To achieve a higher level of energy performance, the project must obtain certification under programs such as DOE Efficient New Homes, PHIUS/PHI or EGC+.
entries.source_title: 2027-28 QAP, Third Draft (posted September 11, 2026; not adopted)

entries.title: Comfort, air and extreme weather
entries.finding: The Energy Office says Colorado's model low energy and carbon code improves indoor air through better ventilation and keeps efficient buildings more resistant to extreme temperatures.
quotes: will also improve indoor air quality by improving ventilation
the code will enhance climate resilience as more energy efficient buildings are more resistant to extreme temperatures
entries.source_title: Colorado's New Model Low Energy and Carbon Code (press release)

entries.title: An efficient building can carry a lower utility allowance
entries.finding: Tax credit rent caps include a utility allowance for tenant-paid utilities, so a lower allowance leaves more rent for the owner. CHFA lets owners use an engineer's Energy Consumption Model, which reflects the building actually designed, instead of the housing authority's schedule.
quotes: must use one of the following four sources: Applicable Public Housing Authority, Actual Usage and Rate Estimate, HUD Utility Schedule Model, or Energy Consumption Model.

entries.title: Solar can lower the electric allowance
entries.finding: Where residents are billed by submeter, the expected credit from on-site solar or a community solar garden can be counted in the electric allowance in year one, using the Energy Consumption Model.
quotes: the projected annual CSG credit or on-site solar credit may be incorporated into the utility allowance for electricity by using the Energy Consumption Model (ECM, Option 4) in the first year of the project.

entries.title: Garden subscriptions stay with the owner
entries.finding: The cost of a community solar garden subscription cannot be passed to tenants.
quotes: It is important to note that the cost of the CSG subscription cannot be passed onto the tenant.

entries.title: Large buildings must benchmark and improve
entries.finding: Building Performance Colorado (HB21-1286) covers commercial, multifamily and public buildings of 50,000 square feet or more: annual energy benchmarking and performance targets.
quotes: statute (HB21-1286) was adopted and put into effect in 2023 and requires owners of commercial, multifamily, and public buildings 50,000 square feet or larger to annually benchmark their whole-building energy use and meet set building performance targets.

entries.title: The targets and the date
entries.finding: The goal is 7% lower emissions from these buildings by 2026 and 20% by 2030, against 2021. Benchmarking reports and fees are due each November 1.
quotes: reduce emissions from the commercial buildings sector by 7% by 2026 and 20% by 2030, compared to 2021 levels.
November 1, annually: Benchmarking report and fee payment due. Late reports and fees are subject to penalties.

entries.title: EGC and LEED cost more to build than NGBS
entries.finding: EGC and LEED require ENERGY STAR Multifamily New Construction, whose above-code systems and construction testing often raise cost. CHFA's hub gives no Colorado cost premium; price it with your contractor and rater.
quotes: LEED and EGC both require ENERGY STAR building certification for new construction. The ENERGY STAR Multifamily New Construction (MFNC) certification is a rigorous energy standard that results in better energy performance. The standard imposes above code minimum system requirements and construction phase testing that often increases project cost.
entries.publisher: CHFA Colorado Multifamily Affordable Housing Electrification Hub

entries.title: NGBS fits a tight budget under an older code
entries.finding: NGBS's energy chapter uses the 2018 IECC as its baseline, so in a town on the 2018 code or older it is often the lower-cost certification to reach. It is still a full certification with its own required practices and points, not code compliance, so budget for it.
quotes: The current version of the NGBS (2020) Energy Chapter references the 2018 IECC as a baseline.
Projects that have tight construction budgets and are located in a jurisdiction that has adopted the 2018 IECC or older may want to consider NGBS certification.
entries.publisher: CHFA Colorado Multifamily Affordable Housing Electrification Hub

entries.title: Under the 2021 code, the gap narrows
entries.finding: The 2021 IECC asks more of every building, so the extra cost of ENERGY STAR (and so EGC or LEED) is smaller there.
quotes: The 2021 IECC increased energy requirements compared to previous versions. As a result, there is less of a cost difference between systems required by the energy code and those required by ENERGY STAR MFNC.
entries.publisher: CHFA Colorado Multifamily Affordable Housing Electrification Hub

entries.title: Your town's code sets the baseline
entries.finding: Under HB22-1362, a town or county that updated its building codes between July 1, 2023 and July 1, 2026 had to adopt an energy code at least as strong as the 2021 IECC plus the state's electric-ready and solar-ready language. One that updates after July 1, 2026 must match the model low energy and carbon code or better.
quotes: THE GOVERNING BODY OF A MUNICIPALITY THAT HAS ADOPTED AND ENFORCED ONE OR MORE BUILDING CODES, AND THAT UPDATES ONE OR MORE BUILDING CODES ON OR AFTER JULY 1, 2023, AND BEFORE JULY 1, 2026, SHALL ADOPT AND ENFORCE AN ENERGY CODE THAT ACHIEVES EQUIVALENT OR BETTER ENERGY PERFORMANCE THAN THE 2021 INTERNATIONAL ENERGY CONSERVATION CODE AND THE MODEL ELECTRIC READY AND SOLAR READY CODE LANGUAGE

UPDATES ONE OR MORE BUILDING CODES ON OR AFTER JULY 1, 2026, SHALL ADOPT AND BEGIN ENFORCING AN ENERGY CODE THAT ACHIEVES EQUIVALENT OR BETTER ENERGY AND CARBON EMISSIONS PERFORMANCE THAN THE MODEL LOW ENERGY AND CARBON CODE
entries.source_title: HB22-1362 as enacted (municipal and county code sections)

entries.title: Small rural counties can lag
entries.finding: A county of fewer than thirty thousand people may stay on one of the last three IECC editions if it applied for, and did not get, a state code-adoption grant.
quotes: A RURAL COUNTY MEANS A COUNTY WITH A POPULATION OF LESS THAN THIRTY THOUSAND PEOPLE
IS REQUIRED TO ADOPT AND ENFORCE AN ENERGY CODE THAT ACHIEVES EQUIVALENT OR BETTER ENERGY PERFORMANCE THAN ONE OF THE LAST THREE MOST RECENT EDITIONS OF THE INTERNATIONAL ENERGY CONSERVATION CODE

entries.title: The new code does not require all-electric
entries.finding: The model low energy and carbon code became the state minimum on July 1, 2026. It does not mandate electrification; all-electric and mixed-fuel buildings both have a path, and solar-ready, electric-ready and EV-ready rules stay.
quotes: becomes Colorado's new minimum energy code on July 1, 2026
While the code does not mandate electrification
The code maintains existing requirements for new construction to be solar-ready, electric-ready and EV-ready.
entries.source_title: Colorado's New Model Low Energy and Carbon Code (press release)

entries.title: Metering moves the bills and the allowance
entries.finding: A master meter with owner submeters usually lands on a commercial rate at least 20% below one utility meter per apartment, and the metering choice can move utility allowances by 20% or more. Submetering also puts billing and collections on the owner.
quotes: reduced meter fees typically result in an effective building rate that is at least 20% less than projects with residential utility meters for each apartment.
the metering approach can impact utility allowance values by 20% or more.
entries.publisher: CHFA Colorado Multifamily Affordable Housing Electrification Hub

entries.title: Ratio billing is allowed again, with conditions
entries.finding: CHFA's Utility Allowance Policy says HB25-1090 banned ratio utility billing (RUBS) from January 2026. HB26-1013, approved March 26, 2026, allows it again if the total billed to tenants does not exceed the utility's bill for the property, there is no markup or fee, common-area costs are left out, and the lease discloses the method. Buildings whose permits are applied for on or after July 1, 2027 must have every unit's gas, electric and water metered by the utility or a submeter.
quotes: THIS SECTION DOES NOT PROHIBIT A LANDLORD OR LANDLORD'S AGENT FROM ALLOCATING UTILITY COSTS AMONG TENANTS OF THE SAME RESIDENTIAL PREMISES USING A RATIO UTILITY BILLING SYSTEM IF:
THE AGGREGATE AMOUNT BILLED TO ALL TENANTS OF THE RESIDENTIAL PREMISES DOES NOT EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNT CHARGED BY THE UTILITY PROVIDER FOR SERVICE TO THE ENTIRE RESIDENTIAL PREMISES
THE UTILITY COSTS FOR COMMON AREAS OR SHARED FACILITIES AT THE RESIDENTIAL PREMISES ARE EXCLUDED FROM ANY TENANT ALLOCATION

FOR RESIDENTIAL PREMISES CONSTRUCTED WITH PERMITS APPLIED FOR ON OR AFTER JULY 1, 2027, GAS, ELECTRIC, AND WATER UTILITY SERVICE DELIVERED TO A RESIDENTIAL PREMISES MUST BE METERED EITHER DIRECTLY BY THE UTILITY PROVIDER OR BY A SUBMETER.
Approved: March 26, 2026
Colorado House Bill 25-1090: Protections Against Deceptive Pricing Practices, effective 01.01.2026, now prohibits the use of RUBS by landlords.

also_see.title: CHFA Utility Allowance Policy (effective 10.20.2025), which predates HB26-1013

entries.title: Start the allowance model early
entries.finding: An engineer's model or HUD's model needs CHFA's preliminary approval 60 to 90 days before the tax credit application, unless the allocation plan says otherwise. The Third Draft's redline changes the number of days, so check the adopted plan.
quotes: Applicants relying on the HUD Utility Schedule Model or the Energy Consumption Model

to CHFA’s Multifamily Program Compliance department 60 to 90 days prior to the Housing Tax Credit or CHFA Multifamily Loan application submission date, unless otherwise specified in an allocation plan.

entries.title: Electrifying an existing building can raise bills
entries.finding: In a retrofit, new loads can change the rate class and raise monthly costs, and can move costs between owner and residents. Check panel, feeder and transformer capacity first.
quotes: changes in load profiles can alter utility tariffs and increase monthly expenses. In addition, electrification can shift how energy costs are allocated between owners and residents.
entries.publisher: CHFA Colorado Multifamily Affordable Housing Electrification Hub

entries.title: 45L new energy efficient home credit
entries.finding: Ends for homes acquired after June 30, 2026. CHFA's hub still suggests pairing EGC or LEED with 45L; that no longer applies to new projects.
quotes: Section 45L(h) is amended by striking ``December 31, 2032'' and inserting ``June 30, 2026''.

entries.title: 179D efficient commercial building deduction
entries.finding: Does not apply to property whose construction begins after June 30, 2026.
quotes: Section 179D is amended by adding at the end the following new subsection: ``(i) Termination.--This section shall not apply with respect to property the construction of which begins after June 30, 2026.''.

entries.title: 48E clean electricity credit: solar and wind
entries.finding: Solar or wind placed in service after December 31, 2027 gets no 48E credit. The cutoff reaches only projects that began construction more than 12 months after the law was enacted; earlier starts keep the old rules. Battery storage is excepted.
quotes: This section shall not apply to any qualified property placed in service by the taxpayer after December 31, 2027, which is part of an applicable facility.
This paragraph shall not apply with respect to any energy storage technology which is placed in service at any applicable facility.
The amendments made by subsection (a) shall apply to facilities the construction of which begins after the date which is 12 months after the date of enactment of this Act.

entries.title: 48E low-income bonus for solar on affordable housing
entries.finding: Solar on a qualifying affordable rental building can earn 20 more percentage points, but only with an IRS capacity allocation, and only inside the solar cutoff above. Whether any allocation remains was not confirmed.
quotes: in the case of a facility described in subclause (II) of paragraph (2)(A)(iii), 20 percentage points
is part of a qualified low-income residential building project or a qualified low-income economic benefit project.

entries.title: Section 48 energy credit (the old ITC)
entries.finding: Closed to solar and most other energy property whose construction began on or after January 1, 2025; 48E replaced it.
quotes: but only with respect to property the construction of which begins before January 1, 2025

entries.title: Solar for All (EPA)
entries.finding: EPA stopped the program and the 2025 tax law rescinded its remaining funds. Do not count Colorado's award as available money; check for court rulings before relying on that.
quotes: On August 7, 2025, Administrator Zeldin announced the agency will no longer be implementing the $7 billion Solar for All program to remain aligned with Congressional intent. The Working Families Tax Cut repealed EPA’s authority to administer the program and rescinded all remaining funds.

entries.title: Colorado heat pump tax credit
entries.finding: Claimed by a registered contractor, who passes part of it to you as a discount on the invoice. For 2026 installations: $1,000 per air-source heat pump, $2,000 ground- or water-source, $250 per heat pump water heater. A heat pump serving several apartments earns one credit per unit served.
entries.fits: New construction and rehab, any utility territory
entries.caveat: Amounts drop again in tax year 2029.
quotes: 2026 Tax Credit and Discount Amounts (installed on or after January 1, 2026)
Air-Source: $1,000 (minimum customer discount $333). Ground-source, water-source, or combined-source: $2,000 ($667). Water Heater: $250 ($83).
a registered contractor may claim one tax credit for each unit served by that heat pump.
The total tax credit amounts will decrease again in tax year 2029, which will impact customer discount amounts.
entries.source_title: Colorado Heat Pump Tax Credits (2026 table)

entries.title: Xcel Energy Design Assistance
entries.finding: Free energy modeling and rebates for new buildings or major renovations over 20,000 square feet, for Xcel business customers still in schematic or early design. CHFA lists it in the QAP.
entries.fits: New construction or major rehab in Xcel territory
entries.caveat: Xcel's information sheet carries no date and sets incentives against an older baseline; confirm current terms with Xcel.
quotes: Xcel Energy business customer (excluding natural gas transport customers)
Project size is more than 20,000 square feet
Project status is in Schematic or Early Design phase

entries.title: Xcel Multifamily Building Efficiency
entries.finding: A no-cost assessment and free in-unit products for existing buildings of five or more apartments, market rate or income qualified.
entries.caveat: CHFA's listing dates from 2023; confirm current terms with Xcel.
quotes: No-cost services include: Identifying energy-saving opportunities through an onsite assessment
Properties have five or more units per building; Market rate and income qualified buildings are eligible.
Last Updated: 09/18/2023
entries.source_title: Multifamily Building Efficiency Program (CHFA Resource Finder listing)
entries.publisher: CHFA Colorado Multifamily Affordable Housing Electrification Hub

entries.title: Co-op and municipal utility rebates
entries.finding: CHFA's Colorado Resource Finder lists rebates and loans by utility, including rural electric co-ops such as Poudre Valley REA, United Power, Holy Cross Energy, La Plata Electric, San Miguel Power, San Luis Valley REC, White River and Y-W Electric. Amounts change yearly; call the utility.
entries.fits: Any deal outside Xcel territory, or gas service from another utility
quotes: Explore funding, financing, and incentive opportunities available to help electrify your new construction or rehabilitation.
entries.publisher: CHFA Colorado Multifamily Affordable Housing Electrification Hub

entries.title: Energy Outreach Colorado multifamily program
entries.finding: Assessment, funding help, project management and inspection for efficiency upgrades in existing affordable buildings where at least 66% of units house residents at or below 80% of AMI. New construction is not eligible now. CHFA lists it in the QAP.
quotes: Your multifamily property must have at least 66% of units occupied by residents earning at or below 80% of the Area Median Income (AMI). New construction is not currently eligible for funding.

entries.title: Home Energy Rebates (federal IRA, run by the Energy Office)
entries.finding: Colorado's versions of the Inflation Reduction Act HOMES and HEEHRA rebates. The single-family appliance rebate is closed in both regions; the Energy Office says small multifamily rebates come in 2026, with no opening date confirmed.
entries.fits: Existing small and large multifamily, once open
entries.caveat: Federally funded; do not count on it until the Energy Office opens the multifamily phase.
quotes: The HEAR single-family program is now closed for both Region 1 (the Front Range) and Region 2 (All Other Counties). Rebates for small multifamily buildings will be available in 2026.
entries.source_title: Home Energy Rebates (as read for this site's funding tracker)

entries.title: High-efficiency electric heating and appliances grants
entries.finding: HB22-1362 lets the Energy Office grant money to housing developers, among others, for electric heating in several buildings within a neighborhood. No open round was confirmed.
quotes: HIGH-EFFICIENCY ELECTRIC HEATING AND APPLIANCES GRANT PROGRAM TO PROVIDE GRANTS TO INSTITUTIONS OF HIGHER EDUCATION, LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, UTILITIES, NONPROFIT ORGANIZATIONS, BUSINESSES AND OTHER ENTITIES AS DETERMINED BY THE COLORADO ENERGY OFFICE, AND HOUSING DEVELOPERS FOR THE INSTALLATION OF HIGH-EFFICIENCY ELECTRIC HEATING EQUIPMENT IN MULTIPLE STRUCTURES WITHIN A NEIGHBORHOOD.

entries.title: Large Building Decarbonization Showcase
entries.finding: Grants of $500,000 to $2 million, covering 50 to 65% of implementation costs, for existing buildings covered by Building Performance Colorado. Round 2 applications are due by October 23, 2026; no later round is announced.
entries.fits: Existing buildings covered by Building Performance Colorado
quotes: Amount: $500,000 - $2 million per award; 50 - 65% of the implementation costs up to $2 million with $8.5m in total funding available. Application Rounds: The deadline for Round 2 has been extended to October 23, 2026. Round 2 covers implementation only projects.
entries.source_title: Large Building Decarbonization Showcase Grant Program (as read for this site's funding tracker)

entries.title: Collective Clean Energy Fund (CCEF) loans
entries.finding: Colorado's nonprofit clean energy lender, formerly the Colorado Clean Energy Fund, lends to property owners and developers for efficiency, heat pumps, solar, storage and EV charging. Its rates have ranged from 2.5% to 7.75%.
entries.fits: Gap financing for upgrades, new or existing
entries.caveat: CHFA's hub still lists a CCEF Clean Affordable Multifamily Housing Fund. CCEF's own page says its commercial products were updated and does not name it; ask CCEF.
quotes: Our loan offerings are designed to address finance gaps for clean energy and energy efficiency improvements that result in reduced greenhouse gas emissions and increased electrification.
Historically, our interest rates have ranged from 2.5% to 7.75% depending on the project details.

entries.title: Colorado C-PACE
entries.finding: Long-term financing, up to 20 years and up to 100% of improvement costs, for efficiency, renewable, water and resilience work on multifamily buildings of 5 or more units, new or existing. Repaid through a property assessment, so bring your lender and investor in early.
quotes: Multifamily (5 units or more)
Property owners can use financing for both existing and newly constructed buildings.
Owners can select long-term financing (up to 20 years) for as much as 100% of improvement costs.
